rows.text: The primitive SHALL permit at most one terminal transition (value, error, abandon or cancel) per future.
The primitive SHALL deliver a terminal outcome to at most one receiver, independently of how the producer resolved.
A value resolution SHALL be refused with TYPE_MISMATCH unless the value is an instance of the declared value type; bool SHALL NOT satisfy a non-bool type.
An error resolution SHALL carry a non-empty message of at most 4096 characters and SHALL be delivered as the tagged outcome ("error", message), not raised.
Taking an abandoned future SHALL raise FUTURE_ABANDONED and SHALL consume receiver ownership.
A resolution attempted after abandonment SHALL be refused with FUTURE_ALREADY_RESOLVED and SHALL NOT change state.
A second resolution SHALL be refused with FUTURE_ALREADY_RESOLVED and SHALL NOT overwrite the first.
A second receiver SHALL be refused with FUTURE_ALREADY_TAKEN, including after the governed runtime released the future (within the tombstone window).
Malformed payloads or errors SHALL be refused without changing state; state-machine refusals SHALL take precedence over argument refusals.
Under simultaneous resolution attempts exactly one SHALL succeed.
Under simultaneous receiver attempts exactly one SHALL obtain the outcome.
A value written by the resolving thread before resolve returns SHALL be visible to the receiving thread that observes it (lock-based happens-before).
Receiver cancellation SHALL be terminal; a later resolution SHALL be refused with FUTURE_CANCELLED.
Dropping the last resolver capability of a pending governed future SHALL abandon it.
Waiting with a caller timeout SHALL NOT change the future's state.
A resolver capability SHALL NOT permit take; a receiver capability SHALL NOT permit resolution; an observer SHALL NOT mutate or consume.
Cross-tenant access SHALL be refused with PERMISSION_DENIED indistinguishable from a non-existent future.
The wire boundary SHALL authenticate every request before reading or mutating state and SHALL reject missing, malformed, forged, expired, replayed, wrong-issuer and wrong-audience credentials.
Secrets and raw payloads SHALL NOT appear in logs, error records, audit events or evidence.
Core modules SHALL perform no filesystem, network, subprocess or environment access.
Administrative controls SHALL require the runtime's AdminCap and SHALL be audited.
Security-sensitive events SHALL be recorded in a tamper-evident chain whose verification detects mutation and deletion.
Unavailable identity, key or trusted-time services SHALL cause the wire boundary to fail closed.
Admission SHALL refuse new futures with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED at the process and tenant hard limits before allocation.
A terminal, consumed future SHALL be released from the registry.
Measured latency, throughput and memory SHALL stay within conformance/PERFORMANCE_THRESHOLDS.json on the reference environment.
A release SHALL be blocked when the regression gate detects an unwaived regression against the approved baseline.
Status SHALL expose version, state, readiness, reasons, config revision, contract versions, capabilities, dependencies and limits per PK_FUTURE_STATUS/1.
Configuration SHALL be validated as a whole and activation SHALL fail closed and be atomic.
An operator or failed health check SHALL be able to restore the last-known-good configuration.
The component SHALL support drain and freeze quarantine at component and tenant scope.
Declared metrics SHALL be emitted with bounded label cardinality.
Logs SHALL follow PK_FUTURE_LOG/1 with trace and config identifiers and redaction.
Wire documents SHALL be validated strictly against versioned schemas; another major SHALL be refused with INCOMPATIBLE_VERSION.
Unknown error codes from newer peers SHALL map to UNKNOWN preserving the original code.
The release gate SHALL treat a skipped mandatory test as BLOCKED, never PASS.
